Dear The Daily Historian,

I wanted to follow up on my earlier messages because I encourage you not to delete the X thread you have built on the Leo Frank case. It has reached a large audience, and I think it can serve as a stepping stone for deeper research rather than an endpoint.

I also think your thread is very useful because it shows how powerful institutional forces on one side of the case have cultivated the predominant modern narrative surrounding this true crime for more than 113 years. A person encountering the Leo Frank case for the first time today is far more likely to encounter the defense-side story of an innocent Jewish man destroyed by Southern antisemitism than a careful examination of the evidence presented during the 1913 trial, the state appeals, the federal litigation, the commutation, and the later pardon.

For generations, what I call the multigenerational cult of Leo Frank, whose most committed adherents are often called Frankites, has worked to rehabilitate Frank as a civil rights martyr of antisemitism and a symbol of wrongful conviction. I do not use “cult” to describe every person who believes Frank was innocent. I use it to describe an advocacy culture in which a conclusion is treated as sacred, repeated across generations, and protected through books, newspapers, universities, documentaries, plays, memorials, historical markers, organizations, websites, educational guides, and legal advocacy.

I have encountered people who refuse to seriously consider the prosecution side of the case, regardless of what evidence is presented to them. They treat questioning the predominant Frank narrative almost as a kind of sacrilege. I believe discussion of the Leo Frank case should include both sides, the evidence, skepticism, and open debate.

From my decades of reading, the lion’s share of influential modern books I have encountered on this case are sympathetic to Frank and hostile toward the verdict. Many seek to persuade the reader of his innocence rather than give the prosecution’s evidence, the trial record, and the appellate record equal weight.

My objection is not to anyone arguing for Frank’s innocence. People have every right to make such an argument. My objection begins when advocacy becomes historical orthodoxy and dramatic claims are repeated without a clear source trail.

My own reading of the trial record leads me to reject the claim of a prosecution driven by ethnic Jew-hatred or religious persecution. The State’s case was built around witness testimony, chronology, conduct, physical circumstances, and the prosecution’s theory of the crime. Frank’s Jewish identity was not offered as legal proof of guilt.

Modern organizations such as the Anti-Defamation League reach a very different conclusion and describe the trial as defined by antisemitism. I think readers should examine the record and decide for themselves.

There is also a neglected part of this history involving race. A New York Sun report published Sunday, October 12, 1913, said Luther Rosser introduced Frank’s race during the defense summation. The same report said Rae Frank, Leo Frank’s mother, denounced Solicitor General Hugh Dorsey as “You Christian dog.” Contemporary Atlanta reporting confirms an outburst by Rae Frank, although accounts vary on the exact wording. Members of my own family were present in the courtroom. No epithets were hurled at Leo Frank during his trial, but there were false accusations of antisemitism made by the defense, especially in Arnold's closing arguments. 

The racial language used against Jim Conley in the defense summations and later pro-Frank publicity also deserves direct study. (New York Sun, 13)

The legal record deserves far more attention than it usually receives.

On Tuesday, February 17, 1914, the Georgia Supreme Court affirmed Frank’s conviction by a 4–2 vote in Frank v. State, 141 Ga. 243, 80 S.E. 1016. Justices Atkinson, Evans, Lumpkin, and Hill formed the majority. Chief Justice Fish and Justice Beck dissented. Contemporary reporting of the decision identifies the dissent as focusing on admission of testimony from Jim Conley and C. B. Dalton concerning prior immoral conduct, not on a finding of evidentiary insufficiency. The conviction remained in force. (Georgia Supreme Court, 1)

This is important because modern retellings can leave readers with the impression of a verdict collapsing under appellate review. It did not.

The first Georgia Supreme Court appeal ended 4–2 against Frank. His extraordinary motion for a new trial was later rejected unanimously, and his final state challenge also failed. Readers should study the majority and dissenting opinions themselves rather than rely upon a modern writer’s summary. (Georgia Supreme Court, 1)

The same rule should apply to one of the most famous claims in the entire case, the alleged cries of “Hang the Jew” during the 1913 trial.

I have spent years tracing this story backward.

The antisemitic death threat hoax: What I call the “Hang the Jew” hoax does not first lead me to a contemporaneous Atlanta newspaper report from the July 28 through August 25, 1913 trial. The earliest precursor I have located so far leads into the national publicity campaign for Frank more than a year later.

C. P. Connolly, a former Montana prosecutor and a writer associated with Collier’s, published a two-part article titled “The Frank Case” in Collier’s: The National Weekly. The first installment appeared Saturday, December 19, 1914. The second appeared Saturday, December 26. Collier’s was published in New York by P. F. Collier & Son. Connolly later expanded his work into The “Truth” About the Frank Case. (Connolly, 2)

In Connolly’s later booklet, he described a visit to the office of an unnamed Frank lawyer in Atlanta. According to Connolly, the telephone rang and an anonymous caller threatened the lawyer if Frank escaped hanging. Connolly did not identify the caller, and the lawyer also remained unnamed in the passage. Connolly then claimed many similar anonymous messages had reached Frank’s lawyers.

This is an allegation of an anonymous telephone threat. It is not yet the later image of a courthouse crowd roaring “Hang the Jew” through open windows at the jury. (Connolly Booklet, 3)

The dates need precision.

Connolly’s first Collier’s installment appeared December 19, 1914. The foreword of his later booklet carries a December 22 date. Burton Rascoe’s Chicago Sunday Tribune article appeared December 27.

Measured from the first Collier’s installment, Rascoe followed eight days later. Measured from Connolly’s December 22 foreword date, Rascoe followed five days later.

Then the story expands.

On Sunday, December 27, 1914, Arthur Burton Rascoe, writing under the byline Burton Rascoe, published a full-page article in the Chicago Sunday Tribune, page 47, titled “Will The State of Georgia Hang An Innocent Man?” https://t.co/3RvkpgRoLI preserves the article and a transcription. Rascoe was writing for a Chicago newspaper, hundreds of miles from Atlanta, sixteen months after the trial ended. (Rascoe, 4)

Rascoe went much further than Connolly’s anonymous telephone-call account. He claimed spectators inside the courtroom shouted threats toward jurors, including, “You’d better hang the Jew.” He then described a threat of violence against both Frank and the jurors if the verdict went the wrong way. He also claimed threats had been made openly in court and described a public atmosphere of intimidation around the jury. (Rascoe, 4)

This publication sequence does not prove Rascoe copied Connolly, and publication dates alone do not prove conscious fabrication. I cannot know Rascoe’s private intent.

What can be documented is the timing and growth of the story.

A late 1914 anonymous telephone threat in Connolly becomes, within days, a much broader account involving direct threats toward jurors inside the courtroom in Rascoe.

For me, this is where source criticism becomes essential.

Where are the July and August 1913 courtroom reports recording jurors being threatened with cries to hang Frank because he was Jewish?

Where are the names of the men supposedly shouting?

Where are the arrests arising from such conduct?

Where are the contemporaneous juror affidavits describing these cries?

A later account can be true, but lateness increases the need for corroboration.

Decades later, versions of this story became part of the Anti-Defamation League’s own presentation of the case.

The screenshots I sent you preserve an ADL website from the period when Abraham H. Foxman served as national director. His August 18, 2005 article, “Lessons of the Leo Frank Case Still Relevant,” described a boisterous crowd outside supposedly chanting “kill the Jew” and “hang the Jew,” with the cries supposedly audible through open courtroom windows.

The claim continued on the ADL’s later website.

On August 6, 2015, the ADL published a retrospective titled “Hang the Jew, Hang the Jew.” Its opening presents the phrase as the cry of a furious mob outside the Atlanta courthouse and says Frank stood trial for a murder he did not commit. (ADL, 5)

On March 18, 2016, Oren Segal published “Seeking Justice: The Pardon of Leo Frank” for the ADL. Segal calls Frank falsely accused and wrongly convicted, describes the trial as infected by a hostile antisemitic atmosphere, and again refers to furious mobs outside the courthouse shouting “Hang the Jew!” (Segal/ADL, 6)

The ADL’s June 8, 2023 backgrounder, “Remembering Leo Frank,” continues the institutional position, describing the 1913 trial as one “defined by antisemitism.” (ADL, 7)

So we are not dealing with an obscure claim buried in one old book. We are dealing with a narrative repeated across decades by a major national organization.

I believe a claim with this level of influence deserves a source trail reaching as close to 1913 as possible.

A second example is the story claiming half of Georgia’s Jewish population fled the state in the aftermath of Frank’s lynching.

The earliest exact numerical version I have located so far appears in The Tennessean on Sunday, March 7, 1982, during the Alonzo Mann publicity cycle. Sandra Roberts wrote, “In the months following the Frank lynching, half the 3,000 Jews in Georgia left the state.” The Digital Library of Georgia preserves the special section within the Leo M. Frank Collections at the William Breman Jewish Heritage Museum. (Tennessean, 8)

One day later, Monday, March 8, 1982, Wendell Rawls Jr. published a closely related version in The New York Times, saying about half of Georgia’s 3,000 Jews left the state. (New York Times, 9)

The arithmetic is simple.

A population of 3,000 with half leaving implies roughly 1,500 departures.

A claim on this scale should leave a measurable demographic footprint. I want to see a contemporary population survey, synagogue membership records, city directories, migration records, or another documented statistical basis showing a statewide loss near 50 percent.

Repetition by later writers does not substitute for demographic evidence.

This becomes especially important because the same general claim later entered federal litigation.

On March 30, 2018, the Anti-Defamation League, Jewish Council for Public Affairs, T’ruah, Union for Reform Judaism, Central Conference of American Rabbis, and Women of Reform Judaism filed an amicus curiae brief in Trump v. Hawaii, No. 17-965, in the Supreme Court of the United States.

The brief describes Frank as convicted after a trial “marked by overt anti-Semitism.” Its footnote then says armed mobs ran through Atlanta, Jewish businesses closed, and about half of Georgia’s Jewish population fled. The footnote cites Wendell Rawls Jr.’s March 8, 1982 New York Times article and Leonard Dinnerstein’s New Georgia Encyclopedia entry. (ADL Amicus Brief, 10)

This is what concerns me about citation chains.

A numerical statement appears in journalism in 1982. A similar formulation appears the next day in another newspaper. Decades later, the claim enters a Supreme Court amicus brief and acquires the appearance of settled historical fact.

I believe a claim used at such a level deserves direct demographic proof.

I want to be precise about Jim Conley as well.

The 2018 Trump v. Hawaii brief does not accuse Conley of murdering Mary Phagan. His name does not appear in the relevant Leo Frank passage. ADL material elsewhere does point readers toward the Conley theory.

The ADL’s 2009 People v. Leo Frank Teacher’s Guide identifies Alonzo Mann as an office boy who, sixty-nine years after the trial, pointed to Jim Conley as the murderer. The same guide describes Mann’s 1982 affidavit as claiming he saw Conley carrying Mary Phagan’s body. It also reproduces Frank’s post-conviction accusation naming Conley as the killer. (ADL Teacher’s Guide, 11)

Even more revealing, the same ADL guide acknowledges racial tactics used by Frank’s side and its supporters. On page 32, it says Frank and his defense resorted to racial typecasting and reproduces racial language used against Conley. On page 52, it says Frank’s defense and much pro-Frank media coverage relied on stereotypes of African-American men as savage, animalistic, and sexually violent. On page 57, it says Jewish members of the press employed bias and African-American stereotypes in efforts to shift blame toward Jim Conley. (ADL Teacher’s Guide, 11)

This deserves far more attention.

One cannot responsibly tell the history of prejudice in this case while examining only prejudice directed toward Frank by Tom Watson in 1914 and 1915. Race was also used as a weapon against Negro witnesses and suspects. Jim Conley and Newt Lee were real people living within the racial order of Georgia in 1913.

Any honest study of prejudice in this case needs to examine both directions.

There is another point people should understand about the later pardon attempts of 1983 and 1986. 

In December 1983, the Georgia State Board of Pardons and Paroles considered a posthumous pardon request to full exonerate Leo Frank, declare him innocent and vacate his conviction, built around the Alonzo Mann material and declined to grant it.

On March 11, 1986, the Board granted a different pardon without deciding guilt or innocence. The Board expressly wrote, “Without attempting to address the question of guilt or innocence,” and based the pardon on Georgia’s failure to protect Frank while he was in state custody and its failure to bring his killers to justice. (Georgia Pardon Board, 12)

The ADL’s own 2016 article also acknowledges the 1986 pardon did not exonerate Frank or prove innocence. (Segal/ADL, 6)

I want my own position on the lynching completely clear.

I reject vigilante violence.

I reject extrajudicial lynching.

No private group had the legal or moral right to abduct Leo Frank from the Georgia State Prison in Milledgeville and execute him in Marietta at a former Sheriff's estate. His kidnapping on the night of August 16, 1915, followed by his lynching near Marietta on August 17, was outside the law. People cannot appoint themselves judge, jury, and executioner because they disagree with a governor’s commutation or any other legal decision. (Georgia Pardon Board, 12)

Rejecting Frank’s lynching does not require declaring him innocent. Leo Frank's lynching does not retro-actively make all the evidence at his trial go away. And Leo Frank's religion was not the reason he was extrajudicially hanged. Georgia has historically always been a philosemitic state.

Believing the jury reached a legally sustainable verdict does not require defending his lynching.

These are separate questions.

I also reject transforming the Mary Phagan case into permanent Jew-versus-Gentile ethnic warfare.

I reject antisemitism and racism.

I also reject sweeping accusations of antisemitism used to stigmatize entire communities, generations of Georgians, or every person who concludes Frank was guilty. The Jewish exodus hoax (that antisemitism drove out half of Georgia's Jewish population) is a grotesque defamation, slander and libel of Georgia, and it's people.

In my view, broad hostility aimed at Gentiles is no more acceptable than broad hostility aimed at Jews. I don't believe the Mary Phagan case should be a Jew-vs-Gentile ethnic conflict, even though that part of the story is in the history of the case. 

This is why I keep returning to the same request: go back to the evidence.

Read the Leo Frank Trial Brief of Evidence. Read the Georgia Supreme Court records. Read the motions. Read the majority and dissenting opinions. Read the three Atlanta newspapers day by day during the trial. Read the contemporary national press. I am working toward making all these records available on my website The Mary Phagan Kean Legacy Project (https://t.co/MNvBytB3CS). So far I have the brief of evidence and Georgia Supreme Court records of the Leo Frank trial and appeals. I have more than 2,000 news paper articles transcribed about the case.

Then read Connolly in December 1914.

Read Rascoe on December 27, 1914.

Follow each claim forward and backward through books, advocacy campaigns, institutional histories, educational guides, websites, pardon petitions, and court briefs.

Work chronologically.

Do not begin with a modern conclusion and project it backward into 1913. Do not begin with a conclusion, and then make the evidence fit it. Start with the evidence first and then make a conclusion. 

I wrote the first edition of The Murder of Little Mary Phagan in 1987. I tried to give both sides of the case an equal hearing. I presented arguments used by Frank’s defenders alongside the prosecution evidence because I wanted readers to examine the record for themselves.

I have since placed my 1987 edition in the public domain so students, researchers, and interested readers without the budget for my newer edition can still study my work. My website https://t.co/MNvBytB3CS has over 10,000 pages of primary source material transcribed from the Atlanta press of 1913 through 1915 focused almost entirely on the Mary Phagan case. 

In 2025, I published the second revised edition of The Murder of Little Mary Phagan. It incorporates thirty-eight additional years of research accumulated after publication of my first edition. The book is more than 400 pages long, not quite 500.

I encourage you to keep your X thread. Do not erase it, lets use it as a teaching opportunity.

Use it as a record of the predominant Frank narrative and as a starting point for checking where each claim originated. Challenge my conclusions wherever you believe the evidence requires it. Challenge the Frankite narrative by the same standard.

Ask for dates. Dates anchor a claim in time and space.

Ask for names. Ask the basic questions every careful researcher should ask: Who? What? When? Where? How? Why?

Ask for documents. What is the document called? When and where was it created? Who wrote it, recorded it, or preserved it? Is the author or witness identified, or is the source anonymous? Was it an oral statement later written down, a firsthand eyewitness account, a secondhand report, or a thirdhand repetition? How close was the person giving the information to the event itself?

Ask who first published the claim. What do we know about the writer, newspaper, organization, witness, or institution behind it? Was the person reporting firsthand knowledge, repeating another person, or writing years later?

Ask how close the source was to the event. Geography matters. Time matters. A reporter sitting inside an Atlanta courtroom in August 1913 occupies a very different evidentiary position from a writer hundreds of miles away publishing sixteen months later.

Ask whether a later writer provides a citation. If so, do not stop with the later writer.

Follow the citation backward. Find the original source. Read the entire passage in context. Check the date, place, author, wording, and surrounding material.

Then ask the most important question: Does the original source actually say what the later writer claims it says?

This is how historical claims should be tested. Follow the evidence backward until you reach the earliest source you can verify.

This is also what I mean when I speak of the cult of Leo Frank. I am speaking about the elevation of one historical interpretation into an inherited orthodoxy, where repetition can become a substitute for proof and where criticism of the narrative can be treated as moral wrongdoing rather than historical disagreement. Repetition from either side doesn't make something a fact or settled history.

Travel Style: National Geographic Family Journeys

Trips for adventure-loving families in search of a meaningful way to discover the world together.

Tour Type: Small Group

Group trips average 12 travellers per departure, depending on the adventure. The maximum is usually no more than 16, but some can be smaller or bigger, depending on the trip. Check individual trips for details.

Age Requirements
Minimum age of 7 years for this trip.

Service Level: Upgraded

Quality accommodations and more inclusions than on other G Adventures tours, like meals, private transport, and activities.

Physical Demands: 3 - Average

Some tours may include light hiking, biking, rafting, or kayaking in addition to walking.

---

## **Day 1 – Reykjavík**  
Welcome to Reykjavík! Your included arrival transfer brings you straight to your hotel, where you can settle in and unwind. This evening, meet your fellow travelers during a welcome gathering—an easy, fun chance for families to connect before the adventure begins.

---

## **Day 2 – Reykjavík**  
Begin the day at the Perlan Museum, an immersive showcase of Iceland’s powerful natural forces—from volcanic eruptions to geysers and glaciers. Enjoy a classic Icelandic hot dog lunch, then board a boat for a whale‑watching cruise on Faxaflói Bay. Keep an eye out for minke and humpback whales, playful dolphins, and porpoises gliding through the waves. The remainder of the day is yours to relax or explore Reykjavík at your own pace.

**Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch**

---

## **Day 3 – Hveragerði**  
Journey across a vast lava field and venture into one of Iceland’s longest lava tunnels to witness the inner world of a volcanic eruption. Continue to a traditional Icelandic horse farm to meet the gentle, sure‑footed Icelandic horses—famous for their unique tölt gait. Enjoy a homemade lunch at the farm before hiking through a geothermal valley dotted with hot springs, where you can soak your feet in naturally heated pools. Later, travel to Hveragerði, a charming town built around its own steaming hot spring.

**Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch**

---

## **Day 4 – Golden Circle**  
Visit Þingvellir National Park, where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates slowly pull apart. Stop at a geothermal bakery to watch bread being unearthed from hot black sand—taste it warm and take home the recipe. Continue along the Golden Circle to admire the thunderous Gullfoss waterfall and the famous Geysir hot spring. Spend the evening relaxing, dining at leisure, or soaking in geothermal waters while enjoying the stunning scenery.

**Meals included: Breakfast**

---

## **Day 5 – South Coast**  
Explore Iceland’s cultural heritage, from Viking traditions to early 20th‑century life. Step inside a turf‑roofed dwelling and a historic schoolhouse to learn about Icelandic craftsmanship, architecture, and innovation. Then walk to Skógafoss, one of Iceland’s largest waterfalls, and enjoy lunch at Skógafoss Bistro. This afternoon, wander along one of Iceland’s iconic black‑sand beaches.

**Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch**

---

## **Day 6 – Westman Islands / Vík**  
Sail to the Westman Islands, a volcanic archipelago off the southern coast. Land on Heimaey—the only inhabited island—and stroll among its charming wooden buildings. Discover the island’s dramatic volcanic past, see areas once buried by lava, and hike up Eldfell crater, where the earth still radiates geothermal warmth. Search for puffins and other seabirds nesting on the cliffs before returning to the mainland and continuing to your hotel.

**Meals included: Breakfast**

---

## **Day 7 – Reykjavík**  
Travel back toward Reykjavík, stopping at Seljalandsfoss—one of Iceland’s most photogenic waterfalls. Walk behind the cascade into a misty hidden cave for an unforgettable view. Continue to the Secret Lagoon, Iceland’s oldest natural swimming pool, for a relaxing soak in its warm blue waters. Arrive in Reykjavík and enjoy a festive farewell dinner.

**Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner**

---

## **Day 8 – Reykjavík**  
Depart at your convenience.

**Meals included: Breakfast**

---

Billy Ray is a homeless Kansas man who received an unexpected donation when passer-by Sarah Darling accidentally put her engagement ring into his collecting cup.  Despite being offered $4000 for the ring by a jeweller, he kept the ring, and returned it to her when, panic-stricken, she came back the following day. Sarah gave him all the cash she had in her purse as a reward, and as they told their good-luck story to friends - who then told their friends - her finance decided to put up a website to collect donations for Billy Ray... 

Billy Ray Harris was living on the streets of Kansas City when a woman, Sarah Darling, dropped spare change into his cup. She didn’t realize her $4,000 engagement ring had slipped off her finger and fallen in with the coins. Harris discovered the ring later but chose not to sell it, keeping it safe in case its owner returned.

Two days later, Darling came back in distress, hoping the ring might still be there. Harris immediately handed it back to her. His honesty drew national attention, and Darling and her husband set up an online fund to thank him and help him rebuild his life. Donations poured in from people moved by the story.

The campaign ultimately raised more than $185,000 for Harris. With the support, he was able to secure housing, reconnect with family, and regain stability. What began as a small act of integrity became a widely shared example of trust, generosity, and the impact of doing the right thing even when no one is watching.

Despite the attention he received, Harris often emphasized that returning the ring wasn’t extraordinary to him. He said he had been raised by his grandfather, a minister who taught him never to take what wasn’t his. Long before the viral story, Harris had quietly returned other lost items to people on the street, a pattern of honesty that rarely made headlines but defined who he was.

text:
The ANC has compromised South Africa's strategic autonomy, trading lucrative, institutionalized Western economic ties for ideological fealty to Moscow and Beijing.

This fundamental misalignment has yielded catastrophic, measurable domestic consequences.

A genuine partnership implies a balanced exchange of strategic and economic value. What South Africa has instead is a master-servant dynamic.

China does not view South Africa as an industrial peer; it treats the country as a raw material quarry and a captive market for its manufactured goods.

South Africa continuously exports unrefined minerals, platinum, iron ore, and manganese, and imports high-value Chinese technology, machinery, and consumer goods.

This structural imbalance exports the very industrial multiplier effects, processing jobs, and capital accumulation that South Africa desperately needs to rescue its collapsing labor market.

Alignment with Russia offers absolutely zero macroeconomic utility.

Russia's economy is structurally dependent on the exact same resource-extraction model as South Africa's, making them market competitors rather than natural trading partners.

The relationship exists purely to satisfy the ANC's nostalgic, Cold War-era liberation complexes and to shield Vladimir Putin from global diplomatic isolation on the world stage.

The material cost of this ideological vanity is explicit and devastating.

By cozying up to autocratic regimes, South Africa has systematically alienated the very economic partners that actually keep its grid running and its people employed.

The United States, the European Union, and the United Kingdom combined constitute South Africa's largest export market, accounting for the vast majority of its manufactured and agricultural exports.

The automotive sector in the Eastern Cape, for example, relies entirely on preferential access to Western consumers.

China and Russia do not buy South African cars; the West does.

The state's persistent diplomatic posturing, including refusing to condemn territorial expansion in Europe and ignoring blatant human rights abuses, has pushed its Western relationships to a historic tipping point.

This friction directly triggered severe diplomatic fallout with Washington, culminating in targeted US visa restrictions and ongoing threats to South Africa's lucrative access to the African Growth and Opportunity Act.

The mere threat of losing these agreements has catalyzed aggressive capital flight, depressed the rand, and scared away the billions in foreign direct investment required to fix a shrinking, stagnant economy.

Real sovereignty is not measured by how loudly a country can insult Western powers from a global podium while its own citizens starve. True sovereignty is the clinical, unsentimental pursuit of national self-interest.

A sophisticated foreign policy requires choosing allies based on their capacity to serve South Africa's domestic interests, allies that offer technology transfers, massive capital injection, open consumer markets, and job-creating investments.

When a government actively sabotages its most vital economic lifelines to carry water for Eastern autocrats, it has not achieved independence.

It has simply allowed its foreign policy to be dictated by foreign puppet masters while its own house burns to the ground.

NATO chief wants Europeans to fight American wars
Mark Rutte has justified the US-Israeli war on Iran and said European nations should “take care” of the Middle East in the future
Published 23 Sep, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/50b4AtKKLi
European NATO nations should take greater responsibility for security in the Middle East, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has said. He also defended the US-Israeli war on Iran and argued that European members should spend less on social programs and more on the military.
Rutte made the remarks at a Chicago Council on Global Affairs event in Iowa on Tuesday after being asked to “make the case” for NATO to Americans by explaining “what’s in it” for them.
He described the Middle East as “Europe’s backyard” and “not the United States’ backyard,” arguing that Washington’s war against Tehran was “necessary” but that the US had to launch it because “somehow the Europeans did not have enough capabilities to do it themselves.”
“In the future, what you get from a stronger NATO is that Europeans can take care of their own backyard,” Rutte said.
The US-Israeli war on Iran, launched in late February, caused major friction within NATO as several European members resisted supporting Washington’s belligerence. Spain refused to allow American warplanes to use its bases for the campaign, drawing US President Donald Trump’s ire. Germany and the UK described the conflict as “not our war,” while stopping short of condemning the US and Israel.
Trump has since repeatedly accused European allies of failing to meet their NATO commitments and claimed the bloc “was not there when we needed them.” In April, US War Secretary Pete Hegseth said NATO’s future was uncertain and Washington could not currently reaffirm its commitment to collective defense.
Rutte also argued on Tuesday that the burden within NATO was unfair because European members spend heavily “on pensions and welfare,” while Washington has to devote more resources to weapons but “would also like to spend more on all these other lofty, beautiful items, but they can’t because they have to spend so much on defense.”
He described raising NATO’s defense spending target from 2% to 5% of GDP as “the fairness element” and part of an “equalizing” process. The remarks come as Washington pushes for a reorganization dubbed NATO 3.0, under which European members would sharply increase military spending and production while assuming “primary responsibility for the conventional defense of Europe.”
Rutte also offered to help “protect the United States from threats of Russia” and China and prevent the Arctic “from becoming militarized by the Russians and the Chinese.”
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said last month that Moscow was primarily interested in “preserving the Arctic as an area of peace and cooperation” and accused NATO of “driving the region towards militarization.” His comments followed European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s proposal earlier this year to use increased EU military spending on “Arctic-ready equipment.”

text:
Montel Jackson vs. Ricky Simón

Montel Jackson 
At 34 years old (born April 24, 1992), the 5'10" southpaw (75" reach) from Milwaukee, Wisconsin (trains at Red Schafer MMA & Pura Vida BJJ & MMA under Solo Acosta) enters with a pro record of 15-4. He has 8 KO/TKOs, 1 submission, and 6 decisions. UFC record sits at 9-4. Amateur record was 8-1.

Background and path: Grew up on Milwaukee’s north side near 91st and West Brown Deer. Most of his friends ended up dead or incarcerated. His father, a former kickboxer, was murdered when Jackson was a kid. Wrestling pulled him out. A high school security guard offered to drop a referral if he joined the wrestling team. He stayed with it through City Kids Wrestling Club under mentor Roger Quindel, became an Olympic hopeful, trained at the Olympic facility in Marquette, Michigan, and competed in a Team USA vs. Team Japan invitational. He turned down college wrestling to stay home and care for sick grandparents. When the IOC voted wrestling out of the Olympics in 2013, the Olympic path died. Friend Devondrick Bankston asked him to help with wrestling drills at Red Schafer MMA ahead of a fight with Raufeon Stots. There he met a Puerto Rican grappler known as Gato, who talked him into a BJJ tournament with almost no formal instruction. He won it, transitioned fully to MMA, and turned pro in 2017. Regional run (Pure FC, KOTC, Driller Promotions) went 6-0 with five finishes. DWCS Season 2, Week 1: third round TKO of Rico DiSciullo earned the contract. Eleven days later he debuted at UFC 227 against Ricky Simón and lost a unanimous decision. Nickname “Quik” comes from a job at the Kwick Pantry corner store and from being fast. Brown belt in BJJ. Never been finished.

Strengths: One shot power that is among the most dangerous in the division. Twelve career knockdowns, the most in UFC bantamweight history. Four knockdowns in a single fight vs. JP Buys (division record). 18-second KO of Da’Mon Blackshear. First round KO of Rani Yahya. Long southpaw frame with a 75" reach at 135. Accurate, snappy left hand, check hooks, body kicks, and occasional head kicks. Extremely low absorption rate (1.40 SApM, among the lowest in the division). High takedown accuracy when he actually shoots (63%). Scrambles well enough to stand quickly after being taken down. Durable chin. Has gone the distance repeatedly without visible fade when he chooses to work.

Weaknesses: Output is the career problem. He lands 3.02 significant strikes per minute but often waits for the perfect counter instead of building rounds. That inactivity cost him close splits to Deiveson Figueiredo (outlanded 30-23 but lost the grappling minutes) and Raoni Barcelos (scored a knockdown and outlanded 35-21, yet ate six takedowns and 7:45 of control). Takedown defense is only 67% and drops when opponents chain attempts. He can look coiled and dangerous for long stretches without actually throwing.

Ricky Simón 
At 34 years old (born August 31, 1992), the 5'6" orthodox fighter (69" reach) from Pendleton, Oregon & also Vancouver, Washington (trains at American Top Team Portland, Team Oyama, & Gracie Barra Portland under Ian Loveland and Fabiano Scherner) enters with a pro record of 22-7-1. He has 7 KO/TKOs, 4 submissions, and 11 decisions. UFC record sits at 10-6-1. Amateur record was 3-0. BJJ black belt under Scherner.

Background and path: Born in Pendleton to a tight knit Mexican immigrant family. Three brothers and Ricky all have “Simón” tattooed across their upper backs. Second cousin of former UFC fighter Vince Morales. Started wrestling at nine. At Union High School in Camas, Washington he was team captain as a sophomore, state placer. College wrestling at Clark College did not happen after injuries. Walked into a BJJ tournament at Vancouver Mall on a whim, took third, and committed. Former middle school wrestling coach. Regional run through Main Event, KOTC, Titan FC, and LFA produced an LFA bantamweight title (KO of Vinicius Zani in 59 seconds). DWCS Season 1 win over Donavon Frelow did not immediately earn a contract. LFA title and the subsequent UFC call followed. UFC debut was a technical guillotine of Merab Dvalishvili in the final seconds of round 3 for Fight of the Night. Has a young daughter.

Strengths: High volume wrestling when it is working. 4.49 takedowns per 15 minutes career, 76% takedown defense. Chains shots, body locks, slams, and back-takes. Finishing threat once on top. Can box enough to set entries and has real one punch power when he plants (R1 KO of Javid Basharat with a straight right after a takedown sequence, R2 KO of Raphael Assunção). Cardio has held through three rounds of grinding. Survived a late knockdown and orbital fracture vs. Adrian Yáñez and still got a draw.

Weaknesses: Striking defense and volume against better boxers have become liabilities. Absorbs 3.90 significant strikes per minute. Accuracy is only 42%. Recent wrestling numbers have cratered against higher-level opposition: 0-for-6 takedowns vs. Barcelos, 2-for-11 vs. Vinicius Oliveira while being outstruck 42-96, 2-for-13 vs. Mario Bautista while being outstruck 45-112, 2-for-5 vs. Yáñez while being outstruck 44-71 and dropped late. Has been finished twice (Urijah Faber R1, Song Yadong R5). Last seven UFC results: 2-4-1. The 2018 chain wrestling version that buried Jackson is not the 2025–26 version that cannot hold top position against strikers.

Stylistic Breakdown & Key Matchup Factors

Size & physicality: This is the largest physical gap on the card. Jackson is four inches taller with a six and a half-inch reach advantage and a longer southpaw frame. Simón has to close a huge amount of distance just to wrestle or punch. Jackson’s length was already a problem in 2018, and it is a bigger problem now that Simón’s entries are slower and more telegraphed.

Striking: Jackson is the obvious power threat and the more accurate striker (52% vs. 42%). His left hand, body kicks, and occasional head kick are fight ending tools. Simón’s boxing is more pressure oriented and useful for setting shots, but he eats clean counters on the way in and has been dropped or badly tagged in multiple fights. If Jackson actually throws instead of waiting, the range and power edge is significant. If he waits, Simón can crowd him and make it ugly.

Grappling/Wrestling: This is the entire fight, I feel like this has been a common theme this card. In 2018 Simón landed 7 of 20 takedowns and held 5:35 of control to Jackson’s 0:45. Jackson stood up quickly almost every time but could not stop the next shot. That exact sequence is what I think Simón will try again. The difference is that Simón’s recent takedown success has been poor, and Jackson’s scramble/stand-up has improved since the debut. Jackson’s own wrestling (2.71 TD/15, 63% accuracy) is opportunistic rather than a weapon, but he has shown he can do it and hold when he wants to (11 takedowns vs. Felipe Colares). Edge still to Simón if he can chain attempts the way he did eight years ago. Edge to Jackson if Simón’s first two shots fail and the fight stays at kicking range.

Pace & cardio: Both have gone the distance many times. Jackson’s issue is not the cardio, it is actually using it. Simón’s issue is accumulating damage while chasing takedowns. A high wrestling pace favors the Ricky. A kickboxing pace favors Montel.

Intangibles

Rematch: Eight years ago, Jackson’s UFC debut, which he took on 11 days’ notice after replacing Benito Lopez and lost. The first fight is useful, but they have both changed.

Raoni Barcelos: Jackson knocked him down, outlanded him 35-21, and lost a split after six takedowns and 7:45 of control (9 of 10 media members still scored it for Barcelos). Simón landed zero takedowns in six attempts and lost a clear UD while being outstruck 67-82. Jackson’s version of the Barcelos fight was better, for whatever that may mean here.

Rani Yahya: Simón won a decision in 2019 after two knockdowns and four takedowns. Jackson knocked Yahya out in round 1 in 2023.

Different issues: Jackson’s entire career has been a mix of looking good and bad. The pattern is “dangerous when he lets his hands go, frustrating when he doesn’t”. On the other side, Simón’s pattern is “wins when the wrestling chains, loses when it doesn’t”. Both have struggled with these issues in recent bouts, so which version of each shows up?

Wise Prediction

I assume, Simón will try to recreate 2018: chop the lead leg, change levels early, chain the second and third shots, and turn the fight into a scramble and control grind. Jackson will try to keep it at the end of his southpaw jab and left hand, punish entries with counters and body kicks, and stand up immediately whenever he hits the mat. The fight is decided by whether Simón can land and hold the takedowns before Jackson’s power adds up of finds him flush.

Jackson’s length, one-shot power, improved stand-up, and Simón’s documented recent inability to finish takedowns against strikers who aren’t already compromised give Jackson the more reliable paths. Simón is live if he gets an early body lock or slam and never lets Jackson set his feet. He is in trouble if this becomes a kicking range fight or a late round striking war.

My pick: Montel Jackson by unanimous decision (or KO/TKO in R2 or R3 if Simón keeps walking onto the left hand).

Why? The 2018 result was a version of Simón who completed 7 takedowns and a version of Jackson who was making his UFC debut on short notice. Neither of those versions should be expected this weekend. Simón has gone 2-4-1 in his last seven and has been outstruck and stuffed by Barcelos, Oliveira, Bautista, and Yáñez. Jackson still has the inactivity problem that loses him close decisions, but Simón is a much worse person to be inactive against than Figueiredo or Barcelos as he absorbs far more damage on the way in. If Jackson even moderately increases output from the last two fights, the physical advantages should produce clearer rounds or a finish. Simón’s best path is an ugly, low output wrestling win that looks like that first bout eight years ago. That path is narrower than it used to be.

Best bet angle: Primary lean is Jackson on the moneyline. His size, power, and Simón’s recent wrestling drop off create more winning scenarios than the reverse. Jackson by KO/TKO is a live method if you believe Simón will keep shooting after the first stuffed attempt(s). Over 2.5 rounds is the safer secondary if you expect Simón to force clinch/grind sequences. Simón by decision is the live dog path and requires him to land early takedowns and keep Jackson from standing. Under 2.5 is porbably live only if Jackson times an entry.

3/3

Further efforts by Britain, the UN and the World Bank over the next two years to negotiate a sustainable rural development programme that would meet justifiable political expectations were brushed aside. In September 1999 the Bank Board in Washington approved a US$5 million credit that had been negotiated with Zimbabwean Ministers. 

It was meant to jump-start the planning process and to start up a land acquisition fund for groups of communal area farmers to draw on. I don’t know whether anyone in Harare had dared to tell Mugabe before the announcement. As ever he refused to endorse it and it was never implemented. Turning his back on the outside world he acted alone with the tragic results that The Zimbabwean continues to report. 
 So where did it all go wrong? 25 years ago many of us recognised that the pace of change, beneficial though it was, could not meet the political demands in Harare. But over many years attempts by politicians and civil servants in Harare to reduce the bottlenecks in planning and implementation, to allocate government funds for sustainable resettlement and to negotiate foreign aid to support them, gained little or no support in ZANU(PF), in the Cabinet or in State House.

 Did Mugabe and his circle all along want to allocate land as a means of patronage, not as a route to development? Did they see land as simply a symbolic issue and simply fail to understand its economic importance? Could a more active British policy in the early 1990’s have produced a response in Harare that might have got a programme going again before frustrations boiled over? Could the commercial farmers, rather than hoping to stay forever, have acknowledged their fate and negotiated a phased handover to productive successors? 
 These questions and others are unfortunately academic. The gap between what Britain and other donors were prepared to offer and what Mugabe demanded proved unbridgeable. Rather than compromise he has produced a famine.

Maria Taylor is a singer-songwriter celebrated for her hushed vocals, cinematic atmospheres, and emotionally resonant storytelling — both as a solo artist and as a founding member of Azure Ray. Her forthcoming album, Story’s End, unfolds like a hazy, widescreen narrative, with each song acting as a chapter tracing love, loss, fracture, and the quiet search for solace in the aftermath. Written over several years and shaped by profound personal upheaval, the record finds Taylor expanding the signature elements of her work — bell-like piano, sweeping strings, and intimate lyricism — into something more nuanced, expansive, and ultimately life-affirming. Recorded between her California home studio and ARC Studios in Omaha, Story’s End features collaborations with Mike Mogis, Ben Brodin, Brad Armstrong, Conor Oberst, Nate Walcott, and others. The album gradually arrives at a fragile but powerful sense of transformation and hope. At once journal-like and cinematic, Story’s End offers listeners a space for reflection and consolation, paying close attention to the fleeting moments that quietly give life its meaning.

text:
Been digging into TypeSafe's Jev and I think there's real potential here.  Choice, Score, and Noul give you a common API for expressing concepts over app state and getting typed judgments back, which is a much better primitive than prompt-and-parse.

Before sending it anything sensitive, read the MCA.  A few things stood out to me:

1. "Telemetry" (§4.3) includes "hashes, summary statistics and classifications, metrics, and learnings related to Customer's use," and they can use it "without restriction," including for other products.
2. You grant them the right to process your inputs and outputs "in perpetuity" to derive that telemetry, and it survives termination.  No retention period is published.  As written, that reads like they can keep your inputs indefinitely.
3. The training restriction only covers putting your data itself into a dataset that modifies model weights.  Synthetic data isn't mentioned and derived telemetry isn't restricted, so from my reading nothing clearly prevents generating synthetic training data from your inputs.

That's a concern about the wording, not a claim about what they actually do.  Their privacy policy and docs say they don't train on customer requests, and they offer ZDR for enterprise.  But the contract is a lot broader than the public statements, and broader than what Anthropic or Google put in their commercial terms.

IMO it's worth experimenting with on non-sensitive data.  For anything real, get an enterprise agreement with ZDR, and confirm it covers derived telemetry, not just the raw inputs.

AI Overview
A veiled threat implies harm without stating it directly, and law enforcement treats these hidden or indirect messages as serious criminal offenses if they cause sustained fear or intent to harm.
Understanding Veiled Threats
Definition: A veiled (or implied) threat uses code words, symbols, conditional phrasing, or subtle hints to suggest violence or negative consequences without making an overt declaration.
Legal Status: Courts evaluate the context, history between parties, and whether a reasonable person would perceive the message as a genuine threat.
First Amendment Limits: "True threats"—even when indirect, coded, or directed at law enforcement—are not protected speech under the First Amendment.
How Law Enforcement Handles Them
Digital Investigation: Officers and federal agencies use digital forensics and subpoenas to trace electronic messages, emails, and social media posts.
Context and Pattern: Investigators look at a "history of behavior" or prior interactions to decode implied coercion.
Actionable Reporting: Law enforcement advises victims to save all original evidence, take screenshots, and avoid replying to the sender before filing a formal report.

What is the significance of Judas betraying Jesus with a kiss?
Answer

Judas Iscariot was one of the original twelve disciples who followed and were taught by Jesus. Being in Jesus’ “inner circle,” Judas had a closer relationship to Jesus than most people during His ministry. Judas betrayed the Lord to the Jewish authorities. The pre-arranged signal was that the person Judas kissed was to be arrested and taken away (Mark 14:44). In this way the Son of Man was betrayed with a kiss (Luke 22:48).

In the culture of first-century Israel, a kiss was not always a romantic expression of love; rather, a kiss on the cheek was a common greeting, a sign of deep respect, honor, and brotherly love (see Luke 7:45; Romans 16:16; 1 Corinthians 16:20; 2 Corinthians 13:12; 1 Thessalonians 5:26; 1 Peter 5:14). For a student who had great respect for his teacher, a kiss fell well within the healthy expression of honor.

What really stands out in the mode of Judas’s betrayal is that Judas used such an intimate expression of love and respect to betray Jesus. Judas’s actions were hypocritical in the extreme—his actions said, “I respect and honor you,” at the exact time he was betraying Jesus to be murdered. Judas’s actions illustrate Proverbs 27:6, “Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses.” Often, foes disguise themselves as friends. Evil often wears a mask to conceal its true purpose.

Address by the President of the Governorate
Your Excellency Archbishop LUIGI Renna,

Distinguished Representatives of the Regional and Municipal Institutions,

Your Excellencies,
Distinguished Religious, Civil and Military Authorities,

Dear Guests,
First of all, I wish to express my heartfelt gratitude for the warm welcome extended to me and to the delegation of the Governorate of Vatican City State present here today, as well as for your numerous and heartfelt participation.

The Ninth Centenary of the Translation of the Relics of Saint Agatha is an occasion of the highest significance, in which profound faith, centuries-old devotion to the sacred remains of the Saint, and artistic endeavor—understood in its noblest sense as an instrument of evangelization—come together in one solemn celebration.

The Governorate, which I have the honor to represent, has followed every delicate stage of the restoration of the reliquary bust and the precious Veil with deep devotion and the utmost professional care. This work of extraordinary complexity was entrusted to the outstanding specialist team of the Directorate of Museums and Cultural Heritage, led with dedication and exemplary expertise by Barbara Pinto Folicaldi.

We are fully aware of what Saint Agatha represents for this community. She is not merely its Patron Saint; she is its Mother, its faithful Guardian, its Protectress, to whom the people turn in times of trial. Throughout the centuries, the people of Catania have always gathered around "their" Saint whenever adversity struck. The bond between this fearless witness to Christ—a young woman of unwavering faith, even to the supreme sacrifice of her life—and her faithful remains unbreakable.

For this reason, the conservation work takes on a significance that transcends its purely artistic and technical dimension, touching the deepest chords of spirituality and collective identity. Restoring the original splendor of the sacred reliquary that safeguards the Saint's relics is, in itself, an act of veneration and profound homage to her martyrdom.

Aware that transferring both the reliquary and the relics outside the Cathedral would have involved considerable logistical challenges, we deemed it appropriate to carry out the restoration on site. Thus, the reliquary bust—a masterpiece of fourteenth-century goldsmith's art—was restored within the Archbishop's Palace, in the heart of Catania.

Commissioned in 1376 by Bishop Marziale to the renowned goldsmith Giovanni di Bartolo, the gilded silver bust houses the sacred skull of the Virgin Martyr. The work portrays Saint Agatha flanked by two angels, presenting her with a serene countenance made even more gentle by the rediscovery of its original polychromy.

Over the centuries, popular devotion enriched the sacred image with a remarkable and layered collection of ex-voto offerings. Precious necklaces, gold pendants, enamel ornaments, pearls, brooches, and medallions were removed with the utmost care from the repoussé and chased silver surface. Each jewel was then meticulously catalogued and repositioned on a specially designed bodice fitted to a faithful three-dimensional replica of the reliquary.

Every stage of the restoration was preceded by thorough diagnostic investigations conducted by the Scientific Research Laboratory of the Vatican Museums. The structural and aesthetic conservation work was carried out by the Vatican Museums' Metals and Ceramics Restoration Laboratory, while the Veil—another fundamental object of devotion—was entrusted to the Museums' Tapestries and Textiles Restoration Laboratory.

Thanks to the expert dedication of all the professionals involved and to the exemplary collaboration established between the Archdiocese of Catania and the Directorate of Museums and Cultural Heritage of the Governorate, the reliquary bust is today returned to the veneration of the faithful in the fullness of its original beauty.

On behalf of the Governorate of Vatican City State, I am very pleased to offer the Archdiocese and the entire community of Catania, especially in the period of this Jubilee, a renewed priceless artifact that safeguards the sacred memory of your territory: the living and enduring presence of Agatha, your beloved Patron Saint and a lasting symbol of unity, charity, fidelity, and hope.

Thank you.
Newly Restored Reliquary Bust and Veil of Saint Agatha is presented in Catania, Sicily
July 21, 2026

Unam Sanctam
One God, One Faith, One Spiritual Authority
Pope Boniface VIII - 1302
Bull of Pope Boniface VIII promulgated November 18, 1302
Urged by faith, we are obliged to believe and to maintain that the Church is one, holy, catholic, and also apostolic. We believe in her firmly and we confess with simplicity that outside of her there is neither salvation nor the remission of sins, as the Spouse in the Canticles [Sgs 6:8] proclaims: ‘One is my dove, my perfect one. She is the only one, the chosen of her who bore her,‘ and she represents one sole mystical body whose Head is Christ and the head of Christ is God [1 Cor 11:3]. In her then is one Lord, one faith, one baptism [Eph 4:5]. There had been at the time of the deluge only one ark of Noah, prefiguring the one Church, which ark, having been finished to a single cubit, had only one pilot and guide, i.e., Noah, and we read that, outside of this ark, all that subsisted on the earth was destroyed.
We venerate this Church as one, the Lord having said by the mouth of the prophet: ‘Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword and my only one from the hand of the dog.’ [Ps 21:20] He has prayed for his soul, that is for himself, heart and body; and this body, that is to say, the Church, He has called one because of the unity of the Spouse, of the faith, of the sacraments, and of the charity of the Church. This is the tunic of the Lord, the seamless tunic, which was not rent but which was cast by lot [Jn 19:23- 24]. Therefore, of the one and only Church there is one body and one head, not two heads like a monster; that is, Christ and the Vicar of Christ, Peter and the successor of Peter, since the Lord speaking to Peter Himself said: ‘Feed my sheep‘ [Jn 21:17], meaning, my sheep in general, not these, nor those in particular, whence we understand that He entrusted all to him [Peter]. Therefore, if the Greeks or others should say that they are not confided to Peter and to his successors, they must confess not being the sheep of Christ, since Our Lord says in John ‘there is one sheepfold and one shepherd.’ We are informed by the texts of the gospels that in this Church and in its power are two swords; namely, the spiritual and the temporal. For when the Apostles say: ‘Behold, here are two swords‘ [Lk 22:38] that is to say, in the Church, since the Apostles were speaking, the Lord did not reply that there were too many, but sufficient. Certainly the one who denies that the temporal sword is in the power of Peter has not listened well to the word of the Lord commanding: ‘Put up thy sword into thy scabbard‘ [Mt 26:52]. Therefore, both are in the power of the Church, namely, the spiritual sword and the material. But indeed, the latter is to be exercised on behalf of the Church; and truly, the former is to be exercised by the Church. A veiled threat implies harm without stating it directly, and law enforcement treats these hidden or indirect messages as serious criminal offenses if they cause sustained fear or intent to harm.
Understanding Veiled Threats
Definition: A veiled (or implied) threat uses code words, symbols, conditional phrasing, or subtle hints to suggest violence or negative consequences without making an overt declaration.
Legal Status: Courts evaluate the context, history between parties, and whether a reasonable person would perceive the message as a genuine threat.
First Amendment Limits: "True threats"—even when indirect, coded, or directed at law enforcement—are not protected speech under the First Amendment.
How Law Enforcement Handles Them
Digital Investigation: Officers and federal agencies use digital forensics and subpoenas to trace electronic messages, emails, and social media posts.
Context and Pattern: Investigators look at a "history of behavior" or prior interactions to decode implied coercion.
Actionable Reporting: Law enforcement advises victims to save all original evidence, take screenshots, and avoid replying to the sender before filing a formal report.

What is the significance of Judas betraying Jesus with a kiss?
Answer

Judas Iscariot was one of the original twelve disciples who followed and were taught by Jesus. Being in Jesus’ “inner circle,” Judas had a closer relationship to Jesus than most people during His ministry. Judas betrayed the Lord to the Jewish authorities. The pre-arranged signal was that the person Judas kissed was to be arrested and taken away (Mark 14:44). In this way the Son of Man was betrayed with a kiss (Luke 22:48).

In the culture of first-century Israel, a kiss was not always a romantic expression of love; rather, a kiss on the cheek was a common greeting, a sign of deep respect, honor, and brotherly love (see Luke 7:45; Romans 16:16; 1 Corinthians 16:20; 2 Corinthians 13:12; 1 Thessalonians 5:26; 1 Peter 5:14). For a student who had great respect for his teacher, a kiss fell well within the healthy expression of honor.

What really stands out in the mode of Judas’s betrayal is that Judas used such an intimate expression of love and respect to betray Jesus. Judas’s actions were hypocritical in the extreme—his actions said, “I respect and honor you,” at the exact time he was betraying Jesus to be murdered. Judas’s actions illustrate Proverbs 27:6, “Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses.” Often, foes disguise themselves as friends. Evil often wears a mask to conceal its true purpose.

Address by the President of the Governorate
Your Excellency Archbishop LUIGI Renna,

Distinguished Representatives of the Regional and Municipal Institutions,

Your Excellencies,
Distinguished Religious, Civil and Military Authorities,

Dear Guests,
First of all, I wish to express my heartfelt gratitude for the warm welcome extended to me and to the delegation of the Governorate of Vatican City State present here today, as well as for your numerous and heartfelt participation.

The Ninth Centenary of the Translation of the Relics of Saint Agatha is an occasion of the highest significance, in which profound faith, centuries-old devotion to the sacred remains of the Saint, and artistic endeavor—understood in its noblest sense as an instrument of evangelization—come together in one solemn celebration.

The Governorate, which I have the honor to represent, has followed every delicate stage of the restoration of the reliquary bust and the precious Veil with deep devotion and the utmost professional care. This work of extraordinary complexity was entrusted to the outstanding specialist team of the Directorate of Museums and Cultural Heritage, led with dedication and exemplary expertise by Barbara Pinto Folicaldi.

We are fully aware of what Saint Agatha represents for this community. She is not merely its Patron Saint; she is its Mother, its faithful Guardian, its Protectress, to whom the people turn in times of trial. Throughout the centuries, the people of Catania have always gathered around "their" Saint whenever adversity struck. The bond between this fearless witness to Christ—a young woman of unwavering faith, even to the supreme sacrifice of her life—and her faithful remains unbreakable.

For this reason, the conservation work takes on a significance that transcends its purely artistic and technical dimension, touching the deepest chords of spirituality and collective identity. Restoring the original splendor of the sacred reliquary that safeguards the Saint's relics is, in itself, an act of veneration and profound homage to her martyrdom.

Aware that transferring both the reliquary and the relics outside the Cathedral would have involved considerable logistical challenges, we deemed it appropriate to carry out the restoration on site. Thus, the reliquary bust—a masterpiece of fourteenth-century goldsmith's art—was restored within the Archbishop's Palace, in the heart of Catania.

Commissioned in 1376 by Bishop Marziale to the renowned goldsmith Giovanni di Bartolo, the gilded silver bust houses the sacred skull of the Virgin Martyr. The work portrays Saint Agatha flanked by two angels, presenting her with a serene countenance made even more gentle by the rediscovery of its original polychromy.

Over the centuries, popular devotion enriched the sacred image with a remarkable and layered collection of ex-voto offerings. Precious necklaces, gold pendants, enamel ornaments, pearls, brooches, and medallions were removed with the utmost care from the repoussé and chased silver surface. Each jewel was then meticulously catalogued and repositioned on a specially designed bodice fitted to a faithful three-dimensional replica of the reliquary.

Every stage of the restoration was preceded by thorough diagnostic investigations conducted by the Scientific Research Laboratory of the Vatican Museums. The structural and aesthetic conservation work was carried out by the Vatican Museums' Metals and Ceramics Restoration Laboratory, while the Veil—another fundamental object of devotion—was entrusted to the Museums' Tapestries and Textiles Restoration Laboratory.

Thanks to the expert dedication of all the professionals involved and to the exemplary collaboration established between the Archdiocese of Catania and the Directorate of Museums and Cultural Heritage of the Governorate, the reliquary bust is today returned to the veneration of the faithful in the fullness of its original beauty.

On behalf of the Governorate of Vatican City State, I am very pleased to offer the Archdiocese and the entire community of Catania, especially in the period of this Jubilee, a renewed priceless artifact that safeguards the sacred memory of your territory: the living and enduring presence of Agatha, your beloved Patron Saint and a lasting symbol of unity, charity, fidelity, and hope.

Thank you.
Newly Restored Reliquary Bust and Veil of Saint Agatha is presented in Catania, Sicily
July 21, 2026

After four and a half years together, Daniel and Emma thought they had a pretty clear idea of where their relationship was heading.

They lived in Iowa, had built a life together, and were planning to start having kids in about five years.

Then Daniel got an offer that changed everything.

He currently makes $120,000 a year, while Emma makes $60,000 as a young architect. She had only started her first architecture job six months earlier, but she absolutely loved it. She was finally getting established in her career, and she wasn’t experienced or licensed enough to negotiate remote work.

Then Daniel was offered a job in North Dakota paying $300,000 a year.

The catch? He had only one week to decide.
Daniel was immediately leaning toward accepting.

To him, the difference between $120K and $300K was too significant to ignore. He saw it as the kind of opportunity that could completely change their financial future, especially with children somewhere on the horizon.

Emma saw it differently.

She grew up in Bogotá, Colombia, a city of roughly eight million people. She loved city life and had never imagined herself living somewhere extremely rural.

She had eventually learned to enjoy Iowa because of their life together, her new career, her parents, and the friends they’d made there.

North Dakota felt completely different.
And there was another complication.

Emma’s parents had moved from Colombia to Iowa only two years earlier because of the couple. They had jobs there and had built their own life, even though they could potentially find similar work elsewhere.

Daniel tried to find compromises.

He suggested that Emma could move with him to North Dakota.

text:
Arlington County, contiguous to Washington DC,  cut DUI deals for illegal immigrants. Defendants dodge deportation

Arlington County prosecutors have given breaks to illegal immigrants who face drunken driving charges, hoping lower charges will help them avoid deportation, according to a congressional report labeling the jurisdiction a sanctuary.

Commonwealth’s Attorney Parisa Dehghani-Tafti, a Democrat whose jurisdiction covers Arlington County and the city of Falls Church, said her office takes potential immigration consequences into account when handling criminal cases.

That includes domestic violence cases, the House Judiciary Committee said in its interim report on the county, located just outside Washington.

Arlington has also refused nearly every request to turn over illegal immigrants to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for deportation, House investigators said.

Of 310 deportation detainer requests filed by ICE from January 2025 through May 2026, the sheriff’s office honored two. Both were criminal cases involving judicial warrants. No detainers involving only civil immigration offenses — the usual path for deportation cases — were honored, according to data the committee obtained from ICE.

Among those released were a man charged with assaulting a police officer and a second man with three arrests in Arlington, 19 in Fairfax County and pending charges in Maryland.

“Arlington County’s sanctuary policies threaten public safety and undermine the safe and effective enforcement of federal
immigration law,” the report concluded.

The committee had Ms. Dehghani-Tafti testify behind closed doors over the summer and obtained her office’s internal prosecution policies. The documents included guidelines for leniency toward “Dreamers” — immigrants in the country illegally under the Obama-era Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program — who were charged with drunken driving.

The policy notes that the Department of Homeland Security considers a DUI to be a serious misdemeanor that could prevent a migrant from renewing DACA status and lead to deportation.

“Because of this, we must take an individual’sDACA status into account when developing offers to ensure that, while appropriate sanctions and conditions are put in place to protect the public and prevent future similar behavior, an individual is not deported because of their decision to drive while intoxicated,” the policy reads.

It urges prosecutors to determine DACA status early in a case so they can “do our part to prevent the disproportionate collateral consequences of a DUI conviction for a DACA recipient.”

Ms. Dehghani-Tafti told the committee that her office could offer a “lateral charge” with equivalent criminality but one that would avoid consequences from the Homeland Security Department, according to the committee’s 122-page deposition transcript.

In a statement responding to the report, Ms. Dehghani-Tafti said the report did not capture the tenor of her deposition.

“The authors of this report are confident, but wrong. Wrong about Virginia law, wrong about county policy, wrong about our office’s policies and their impact, and wrong about the cases they cite,” she said.

She said “many” of the cases highlighted by the committee were never raised during her deposition, which focused heavily on her office’s handling of the alleged doxing of former county resident Stephen Miller, White House deputy chief of staff for policy.

“From the start, this was a political sham. The committee refused to hear my testimony in public because open testimony doesn’t let you distort a record,” Ms. Dehghani-Tafti said. “In the end, this process amounts to harassing an independent local prosecutor while providing cover for ICE’s abuses.”
Meanwhile, the Arlington County Board adopted a Trust Policy in 2022 and amended it in 2025 to add a provision that prohibits the county’s police department from “initiating contact with federal immigration authorities.”

“In other words, Arlington County’s new policy protects the worst of the worst of criminal aliens — murderers, terrorists and sex traffickers — from deportation,” the committee said.

The Arlington County Board said the Trust Policy is “grounded in public safety, civil rights and constitutional compliance” and that it is not local officials’ responsibility to assist the federal government on immigration.

“The facts and the law have not changed; immigration enforcement is the responsibility of the federal government and the county’s policies and actions have been compliant with the law,” said the Democratic-led board.
